title: Vampire Hunters VR Stage 0 preparation settings

DiagnosticsEnabled.description: Entry diagnostics only; no VR implementation yet.

SafeMode.description: Preserve flat gameplay. A sibling .cfg.safe-mode marker forces effective true; false does not activate missing VR code.

UiVerticalOffset.description: D-113 vhvr-openxr-host.json: metres along head-local up for running HUD/minimap and paused menus. Default is 15 cm below D-112 (-0.10 m); 0 restores D-108 height. Existing distance/width/centering/rays retained. New height not headset accepted.

EyePreset.description: D-147 vhvr-openxr-host.json: per-eye render size preset. low/normal/high scale EyeWidth/EyeHeight by 0.8/1.0/1.2 keeping the eye aspect ratio; custom uses them exactly (clamped 512-4096). Native swapchains follow the scaled size, so it is the whole resolution setting. Not headset accepted; menu not wired.

PerfProfile.description: D-150 vhvr-openxr-host.json: opt-in engine quality dial, applied once at Initialize and logged before/after (off = the game's own settings, untouched). light/strong lower shadow distance, cascades, shadow resolution, pixel light count, LOD bias and particle raycast budget, and switch realtime reflection probes and soft particles off. Only ever lowers a dial (never raises one above what the game asked for), so it is a quality cost that may buy fps, not a claim. Not headset accepted; menu not wired.

RenderFrames.description: D-095/D-148 vhvr-openxr-host.json: engine frames the eye cameras stay enabled per XR frame. 1 renders once and submits on the next frame; 2 renders a second frame whose result is discarded. Default changed 2 -> 1 by measurement (d147a: median prepToSubmitMs 17.0 vs 8.5 ms, median cycleMs 30.10 vs 22.53 ms at the same eye size). 2/3 remain for A/B.

StartupSkipScenes.description: D-200 vhvr-openxr-host.json: comma-separated, case-insensitive scene names whose camera must never become the eye source. 0.9.3 started OpenXR on the first frame that had a main camera - the intro scene - and the game then destroyed that camera when it loaded the menu, leaving the host submitting from a dead source (black headset, frozen window frames). The default "Intro" makes VR wait, inside the same GameplayWaitSeconds budget, until the game has left the intro. An empty value restores the pre-D-200 behaviour.

StartupSettleSeconds.description: D-200 vhvr-openxr-host.json: the active scene must have been unchanged for this many seconds before its camera is adopted, so a scene that is about to be replaced by a load can never become the eye source. 0 = adopt immediately (pre-D-200). The startup gate clamps to 0..10 so a bad value can only shorten a wait; Initialize refuses an out-of-range value with its own error.

HandPoseFrame.description: D-202 (BUG-202) vhvr-openxr-host.json: the frame the hand/aim pose is composed in. Head = the eye frame (identity) and the shipped default; Anchor = the pre-D-202 behaviour (the game camera rotation multiplied into the hand/aim pose) kept for a single A/B sitting. D-211: the head frame's snap turn is a view-yaw offset, so it no longer needs the Anchor frame to move the picture.

SnapTurnDegrees.description: D-211 (user request 2026-10-20) vhvr-openxr-host.json: right-stick snap turn in degrees. 0 = off, 30 = shipped, 45 = wider step. One turn per stick push (engage 0.7 / release 0.3). In the head frame the turn is a session view-yaw offset applied to both eye offsets and both eye orientations and to the hands/aim base, with the anchor (the player's place in the world) untouched; it resets with every new anchor. Any other value resolves to 30 and is logged. VhvrSettings.exe writes this key; not headset accepted yet.

TurnMode.description: D-213 vhvr-openxr-host.json: right-stick view turn mode. Snap = one step per push using SnapTurnDegrees (0=off/30/45). Smooth = continuous rotation while the right stick is held, at SmoothTurnDegreesPerSecond (120 default), stopping while paused.

SmoothTurnDegreesPerSecond.description: D-213 vhvr-openxr-host.json: full-deflection turn speed for TurnMode=Smooth, 30-240 deg/s (120 default).

TurretCycle.description: D-206 (BUG-204) vhvr-openxr-host.json: what the engineer's build-mode grips send the game as a blueprint step. While the game itself reports PlayerController.is_turret_mode the left grip steps back, the right grip steps forward (one step per grip released outside a chord) and both grips together hold the game's Fire action, which the game's own text names as the build confirm (skill_desc_engineer_1: "Press {action=Fire} to build the turret"). Stick (default) = the pad's left stick + the navigationDirection field; Dpad = <Gamepad>/dpad/left,right + navigationDirection (the Arena map also binds dpad/right to Manual Level Up, so watch that side effect); Special = pulse Special Ability/<Gamepad>/buttonEast, the switch the game's own text documents (forward only, so either grip steps forward); Off = the pre-D-206 map (the grips stay unbound, D-057). Any other value is refused at startup, never defaulted. Grips are unbound outside build mode in every case. Acceptance is a headset observation (docs\playtests\PLAYTEST-D204-TURRET-KO.md); menu not wired.

FlameEndpointVfx.description: D-139 vhvr-openxr-host.json: exact GameAssembly hash/context guarded one-byte visual branch in process memory only. Native Flamethrower VFX uses its own end-start instead of muzzle-forward fallback. Restored on release; no attack, hand pose, particle lifetime/space or file changes. Disable with -NoFlameEndpointVfx. Not game/headset accepted; menu not wired.

FlameEmitterPin.description: D-141 vhvr-openxr-host.json: after the hand correction (and again before each eye culls) rewrite ONLY the Flamethrower vfx_flames_transform rotation to the hand attack aim, and re-apply the last written hand pose on busy/skipped ticks. Fixes the emitter swinging opposite to the head (D-140). No attack argument, damage, particle lifetime/space or file changes; restored on release. Disable with -NoFlameEmitterPin. Not game/headset accepted; menu not wired.

CaptureFirstFrames.description: D-147 vhvr-openxr-host.json: write the frame-30 raw eye/source texture pair for both eyes (4 files, ~74 MB at the default 2064x2208 per eye). Off by default: before D-147 this dump ran unasked every sitting. Harness-requested captures (capture.request) are independent of this flag. Not headset accepted; menu not wired.

MonitorCostProbe.description: D-148 vhvr-openxr-host.json: measurement only. Three windows of 120 submitted frames, aligned to the native timing log: baseline, the gameplay source camera disabled (monitor view off, only the two eye cameras render), restored. Prices the monitor view from copyMs/fenceMs/endFrameMs. The source camera is re-enabled on every exit path. Default OFF; no gameplay state changes.

DeferredGpuWait.description: D-148b3 vhvr-openxr-host.json: opt-in overlap experiment for the submit fence. When on, the two eye copies are issued and released without spinning on the GPU event query inside the submit; their completion proof is taken at the start of the next submit (deferred by one engine frame) or at close. The completion proof is kept, only moved; a proof that cannot be taken is fatal. Default OFF = proven-inside-the-submit. Harness flag -DeferredGpuWait; not headset accepted.

PrepareAhead.description: D-149 vhvr-openxr-host.json: opt-in early frame prep. When on, the native submit prepares the next XR frame itself (xrWaitFrame + xrBeginFrame + xrLocateViews + hands), so the engine never spends a whole frame on a prepare-only pass and the managed phase machine positions the eye cameras in the same frame it learns the frame is prepared. The published frame state is unchanged (state 2 after the submit), the chained call runs the same body (so every stop/budget/empty-frame exit behaves identically) and the prepare event that follows only clears a marker. Default OFF = the measured comparison. Harness flag -PrepareAhead; not headset accepted.

HideHudBackdrop.description: D-112 vhvr-openxr-host.json: existing HUD backdrop rules plus exact Player HUD/Bottom Shadow sprite suppression, restored on release. Does not remove health/blood gauges, minimap, score or combo. Not headset accepted.

StockFireCadence.description: D-111 vhvr-openxr-host.json: start on trigger press only; scoped per-hand held input lets stock Weapon.update own cadence. Requires HandFire. Not headset accepted; no RPM/ammo/damage tuning.

AutonomousHeadAim.description: D-111 vhvr-openxr-host.json: propagate HMD gaze to gameplay camera and its top-arm/passive mounts, preserving independent hand world poses and native targeting/animation. Requires HandAim; not headset accepted.

RenderTimingDiagnostics.description: D-136/D-138 vhvr-openxr-host.json, restored by the D-206 verification (BUG-205): read-only per-camera render timing. Patches Camera.FireOnPreCull/FireOnPreRender with observation-only postfixes, records hand tick/read/applied frame, phase, pose/renderer/particle inventory to <output>/render-timing.jsonl, stops itself after 180 s and never moves a pose, animation, particle or camera. Default ON as D-136 shipped it; harness flag -NoRenderTimingDiagnostics. Evidence is NOT_ROOTCAUSE_NOT_ACCEPTED.

OpenXrHost.description: Opt-in SP5 same-game-device OpenXR bridge. Separate vhvr-openxr-host.json Enabled flag. Offscreen clones preserve flat gameplay; marker or disabled diagnostics prevents start. Simulator-only until headset gate.

StereoCameraCapture.description: Opt-in SP5 prerequisite; offscreen mod-owned camera pair using simulator pose snapshot. Not an in-game OpenXR host. Flag lives in separate vhvr-stereo-capture.json Enabled field; marker or disabled diagnostics prevents start.

x-status: Schema/default mirror for stage0 only; not yet wired to VR menu. Plugin currently uses typed BepInEx config, not this JSON directly.
